doc: Curated teardown audit of NEAT Xianxia (Rust sim + Godot viewer + Python harness). Every score carries file + whyScore + excerpts. Suspicions carry verify:true. Generated by the teardown-audit skill.

meta.name: NEAT Xianxia
meta.conduit: scenarios.toml/CLI options → worldgen → deterministic tick loop (offer → NEAT score → serial apply → domain steps → ledger check) → XNS1 snapshot + XXSAVE34 checkpoint → loopback TCP → Godot decode → render/pick; births feed parent genomes back via crossover+mutation and the save ladder re-enters history through 31 versions; dev.py checks feed pass/fail upstream

contract.label: CONTRACT
contract.blurb: the single source of truth: wire + save + scenario definitions and the one real old-bytes fixture

parts.label: wire/save prose contract
parts.what: Prose contract for the TCP wire (XNC1/XNS1 framing, 16-byte records, 6-bit action IDs, map_layers base64 grids) and the full XXSAVE version history 01→34.
parts.why: The only document binding the Rust encoder, the GDScript decoder, and the save ladder to one description; check_protocol.py enforces its testable claims.
parts.breaks: Prose says 'Action IDs occupy six bits' and 'Current saves use XXSAVE34' — both match code today, but the version-history narrative is hand-maintained against lib.rs:2647-3183; a new version that skips updating the prose leaves no machine-visible drift.
parts.whyScore: Top-level claims (version 2, 52 sensors, 16-byte records, class ≤6) are verified by check_protocol.py:40-77; the 31-version save history has no such parity check.

excerpts.text: Each wire message has a four-byte little-endian payload length. Commands are UTF-8 JSON. Replies begin with XNC1 and JSON. Snapshot payloads begin with XNS1, followed by little-endian version (u16), flags (u16, bit zero means paused), tick (u64), allocated count (u32), sample count (u32), metadata byte length (u32) and, since version 2, animal record count (u32). JSON metadata, sample records, then animal records follow. Each 16-byte sample contains ID (u32), x/y (f32), and four bytes for action/flags, cargo/flags, health/age flag, and home.
Current saves use XXSAVE34 for the merged gameplay features, governance, campsite rumours, water routes and road traffic. XXSAVE33 added road traffic to the release format.

parts.label: contract + toolchain constants
parts.what: Machine-readable [contracts] wire=2/save=34 plus toolchain pins (rust 1.99.1, godot 4.6.3, node 24) and fixture paths.
parts.why: dev.py and CI read these constants; it is the machine-checkable third of the contract.
parts.breaks: Bumping wire/save constants here without the code produces a version the loader rejects — but it is a third hand-maintained copy of values that live in code.
parts.whyScore: Verified live during audit: project.toml wire=2 == encoder `out.extend(2u16..)` lib.rs:3422 and == check_protocol.py:41; save=34 == b"XXSAVE34" lib.rs:2641; old_save fixture header is b'XXSAVE12' matching the filename.

parts.label: real XXSAVE12 bytes fixture
parts.what: A real historical town checkpoint (declared payload 2,409,826 bytes compressed) exercised by protocol_suite, replay and bench.
parts.why: The only checked-in save produced by an actual old binary — the sole end-to-end proof that World::load migrates real bytes, not synthetic ones.
parts.breaks: If a nested type embedded in the v12 reader changes shape, this fixture is the only artifact that catches real-byte misparse — all other versions have no byte fixture at all.
parts.whyScore: Header verified b'XXSAVE12' with declared len 2,409,826; it genuinely exercises the v12 path (check_banks/check_relationships/replay), but it is single-version coverage: XXSAVE04-11 and 13-33 have no checked-in real bytes.

parts.why: Decouples viewer verification from a running sim — the fixture pins the metadata shape the UI reads.
parts.breaks: If snapshot_metadata drops a key the fixture keeps asserting the old shape — it verifies UI code, not producer drift.
parts.whyScore: Exercised by dev.py viewer(): runs urban_ui_check.gd --quit-after 150 headless and requires '"urban_ui":"passed"' in output (dev.py:172-184).

transforms.label: TRANSFORMS
transforms.blurb: the compute units: tick orchestrator, candidate offers, action resolution, domain step modules

parts.label: World::step — 20-phase tick
parts.what: One tick: shelter sync → domestic rules → patch renewal → hunger/health/deaths → governance/civic → market+camp observation → parallel NEAT decisions → serial commit → travel → execute → settlement/life/farm/social/education/urban/banking/relationships/wildlife → explored/water/ports/ships → traffic census → quote refresh.
parts.why: The defined order IS the game rules: death→memory-forget→decision→movement→domain settles in sequence; ARCHITECTURE_REVIEW #4 names write-ownership order as the invariant to preserve.
parts.breaks: Phase order is held only by code order + replay digest tests; swapping e.g. deaths after decisions changes outcomes silently in serial mode — the parallel/serial equality test (lib.rs:3900) and checkpoint_replays_exactly are the guard.
parts.whyScore: Documented ordering contract (ARCHITECTURE_REVIEW.md #4) enforced mechanically by determinism tests at lib.rs:3907-3936; still a single 230-line function whose phases are only separable by reading it.

parts.label: candidate offers → NEAT score → request
parts.what: offer_with_limit enumerates up to CANDIDATES=64 feasible actions per deciding agent (every 10th tick per agent), request() scores them with the agent's compiled brain, filters unreachable targets, applies starving/water-blocked fallbacks.
parts.why: The decision funnel: domain code can only propose; brains rank; physics vetoes. The 64-cap and its admitted/omitted accounting exist because of ARCHITECTURE_REVIEW #3.
parts.breaks: Offer enumeration order determines which families saturate the 64-slot cap; a new offer family placed late is silently omitted on dense towns — candidate_counts records this for watched people only.
parts.whyScore: Dense logic with documented cap (contract README 'Candidate counts map each action to [admitted, omitted] at the main offer limit'); the saturation meter exists but only on the watch path, not globally.

parts.label: execute() + destination() twin dispatch
parts.what: execute() resolves each committed action (movement, exchanges, jobs); travel.rs:destination() independently re-maps the same Action set to movement targets.
parts.why: Two dispatch tables over one enum — every new Action must be added to both or it either never resolves or never routes.
parts.breaks: An action added to execute() but not destination() compiles fine and the agent walks to the default market branch instead of its real target — silent mis-routing; no exhaustiveness check spans both tables.
parts.whyScore: Hand-mirrored dispatch: lib.rs:2233 execute() and travel.rs:1695-1768 destination() enumerate overlapping Action sets with different fallthrough defaults; compiles even when arms diverge.

parts.label: urban.rs — property/firms/contracts
parts.what: Zoned districts, buildings, private firms, leases, evictions, production chains and physically-carried inter-building contracts; largest single domain file.
parts.why: The town economy: gazetting at 500c coffers, 3/3/3 town promotion, wholesale→retail wares with their own conserved ledger (ware_accounts).
parts.breaks: The SKU packing `target = building*32 + sku` (urban.rs:345, 1115) is mirrored bare in lib.rs:1861 (`target % 32`) — an unnamed constant; wares ledger and goods ledger balance separately, so a ware-path bug that mints silently passes the goods check.
parts.whyScore: 2,464 impl lines with 15 comments and 11 panics; constants mirrored into viewer text (main.gd:947 'Gazette at 500 copper' vs urban.rs:436 `coffers >= 500`) though the wire exports wealth_threshold/reserve_threshold (urban.rs:2361) that the viewer ignores.

parts.label: travel.rs — convoys/ships/detours
parts.what: Movement: road-corridor steering, water detours with failure backoff, convoy grouping, port planning, ship sailing, waycamp founding that pushes new Markets at runtime.

parts.label: wildlife.rs — second NEAT pool
parts.what: Five-species ecosystem with its own genomes, innovation registry and compiled brains; data-driven SpeciesDef table; carcass/hunting/grass ledgers.
parts.why: Animals evolve too — a parallel NEAT population with its own registry that must migrate alongside the human one on load.
parts.breaks: The SPECIES table comment says 'Order matters: saved worlds and the wire store species as this table's index' — reordering silently re-labels every saved species and the viewer's WILDLIFE_COLORS/atlas columns.
parts.whyScore: Ordering contract documented in-file (wildlife.rs:11-13) and in contract README (species 0-4); 24% test coverage; species indices also mirror viewer field.gd:59-60 tables — a cross-file ordering mirror, unverified by a parity test.

parts.label: life.rs — lifecycle + genome inheritance
parts.what: People: traits, aspirations, marriage, pregnancy, birth (genome crossover + mutation + compile), childhood, deaths; the evolution feedback edge.
parts.why: This is where the loop closes — births write new genomes back into the pool the decisions read from.
parts.breaks: birth() crossover picks the father as 'fitter' parent (life.rs:1781) — a deliberate asymmetry, but fitness is social, not measured; the genome registry must stay consistent or children's node IDs collide with memory-node IDs at u32::MAX-3..
parts.whyScore: Heavily tested (25% of file is tests covering birth/marriage/goal replay); the crossover call and registry mutation are the load-bearing lines — regression = broken brains, caught by compile() + replay tests.

parts.label: civic.rs + governance.rs — councils/elections
parts.what: Village councils each carrying their own NEAT genome + innovation registry (job boards, graveyards, contracts); governance adds elections, nominations, leadership happiness awards.
parts.why: Collective decision-making: the third genome pool, and its brains migrate on load just like people and wildlife.
parts.breaks: Councils sync to markets count (sync_councils at civic.rs:417) — a market added by camp founding grows a council; per-council `innovations` registries each need migrate_brain_schemas coverage (lib.rs:3199-3205 handles it).
parts.whyScore: Three independent genome registries (world/council/wildlife) all handled in migrate_brain_schemas; councils have unit tests (16% of civic.rs) and governance elections are exercised by the protocol suite.

runtime.label: RUNTIME
runtime.blurb: the orchestrator: CLI modes, the serve loop, command dispatch, snapshot cadence

parts.label: serve() — game loop + snapshot cadence
parts.what: Loopback TCP server: accept one viewer, drain commands, advance sim on wall-clock accumulator or advance_days batches, emit a full viewer_snapshot every 100ms.
parts.why: The live conduit: every player-visible frame and command crosses this loop.
parts.breaks: Every 100ms frame calls viewer_snapshot → full snapshot_metadata (accounts, markets, governance, urban, banking…): ARCHITECTURE_REVIEW #2 — paused viewers still pay full report cost; only the wealth ranking is cached.
parts.whyScore: Watchdog-less loop by design (server); the metadata-rebuild-per-frame cost is a logged review finding partially mitigated (animals→records, map_layers split out, cached leaderboard) but summary() still runs per frame.

parts.label: Command enum + handlers
parts.what: serde-tagged command enum (pause/step/reset/save/load/select/mortality_test/set_persona/add_resource/map_layers…) with bounds checks per command.
parts.why: The only write path into a live world — every viewer button ends here.
parts.breaks: Bounds are enforced (speed 0.1–16, ticks ≤10k, days ≤30, agent < len); a new command without validation inherits the same path — each arm checks itself, no shared policy.
parts.whyScore: Per-command validation present throughout (main.rs:574-634); reset/save/load invalidate wealth cache correctly (lines 638, 656); exercised by check_protocol end-to-end.

parts.label: verify/bench/soak/demos
parts.what: Non-serve modes: verify (steps + save + load + 20-tick serial/parallel replay equality), bench (report JSON), soak (multi-seed run with world digest + extinction tracking), and four seeded demo worlds.
parts.why: The deterministic-verification surface that CI and dev.py consume; soak's digest is the nondeterminism tripwire.
parts.breaks: Replay equality compares Agents + Markets but not every field — a divergence confined to e.g. camp_rumours would pass verify's 'Replay mismatch' check.
parts.whyScore: Built-in 20-tick parallel-vs-serial exact-equality check (main.rs:214-223) plus soak digests per seed (267-298); this is the determinism harness the whole repo leans on.

core.label: CORE
core.blurb: the state authority: World struct, SoA agent pools, conservation ledger, load-time validation

parts.label: World — 45-field fused state+orchestrator
parts.what: The root struct: agents/genomes/markets/patches/roads/ledger/stats + ~20 domain subsystems + #[serde(skip)] checkpoint tails (map, explored, governance, rumours, water, traffic, carcasses, meat_trade…) + the transient Watch debug state.
parts.why: Everything trusts it — all nine domain `impl World` blocks write through it; also the audit's main dual-identity: CORE state + TRANSFORM orchestration + BOUNDARY codec + DOMAIN rules + debug harness in one type.
parts.breaks: Adding a non-#[serde(skip)] field changes the base postcard layout and fails every save ≥v19 (loud, caught by tests — but the append-tail convention is only implicit in the code). Adding a field without a validate() arm leaves corruption undetected.
parts.whyScore: Dual-identity monolith: state authority + tick orchestrator + wire encoder + save ladder + inspector/watch harness share one type and one 3,521-line impl file; module split exists (26 domain files) yet the trunk keeps accreting orchestration. Score the fusion, not the size.

parts.label: Agents — 36-column SoA pool
parts.what: Packed struct-of-arrays: 36 parallel Vec columns (x/y/health/hunger/…/tools/urban_weight) indexed by stable person ID.
parts.why: Cache-friendly decisions for up to 1.2M agents; every column must stay index-aligned with its siblings.
parts.breaks: New column → must be added to empty(), the validate() length table (lib.rs:3223-3261), every legacy reader's LegacyAgents, and the save layout — a missed arm fails loudly at load but silently at first save.
parts.whyScore: Classic SoA fragility held by the validate() column-length table — that table IS the mirror list and it's hand-maintained; legacy_v13 froze LegacyAgents so new columns also need per-version readers.

parts.label: conservation ledger + check()
parts.what: Per-good conservation accounting (minted/transformed/renewed/consumed/built) + coin conservation + capacity bounds, verified by check() on saves, on command steps, and inside protocol snapshots.
parts.why: The physical-feasibility guarantee: nothing is created or destroyed without a ledger entry — the single strongest health signal in the codebase.
parts.breaks: check() runs sub-validates but NOT self.validate() — pool-length/market-count gates are load-only; a runtime-grown inconsistency (e.g. 65 markets) passes check() then fails on reload.
parts.whyScore: Runs every save (main.rs:650), every stepped batch (605), soak every 100 ticks (257), and inside every protocol snapshot (check_protocol.py:50-53 asserting error==0 on all accounts including grass and ware_accounts).

parts.label: load-time validate() schema gate
parts.what: Post-deserialize invariant sweep: all 36 SoA column lengths == n, markets 3..=64, home/cargo_kind bounds, convoy membership bijection, plus 10 domain validate_* calls.
parts.why: The last line of defense for corrupt/old saves — every load ends here before the world runs.
parts.breaks: Bound checks are load-only: nothing stops runtime state exceeding them; a new pool or index column absent from the sweep escapes validation entirely.
parts.whyScore: Genuinely thorough gate (lengths, finiteness, convoy bijection, hill bounds) — but it only runs on load; the markets 3..=64 bound can't be violated by the loader, only by runtime camp founding, which no runtime check caps (verify with travel_module).

domain.label: DOMAIN
domain.blurb: the business rules the system exists to run: market economy, needs, memory subsystems

parts.label: Market quotes + escrow refresh
parts.what: refresh() every 10 ticks: per-market per-good target stocks, bid/ask quotes computed from population deficit, escrow reserved from market coins.
parts.why: The price engine — every buy/sell lands on these quotes; escrow accounting is what keeps money conserved while bids float.
parts.breaks: Quotes regenerate wholesale each refresh — a market's coins are re-escrowed against current population; an accounting slip in cancel_quotes/add silently mints or burns (caught by check()).
parts.whyScore: Integer-accounted escrow math with conservation test coverage; the tuning constants (pop/3, /10, /16 targets, bid cap 8) are embedded arithmetic — balance parameters with no external config.

parts.label: needs.rs — drives and family offers
parts.what: Need priorities (energy emergency → recovery offers, children/home obligations → family offers) that preselect what the brain may rank.
parts.why: Domain-specific preselection happens BEFORE neural scoring — the feasibility shell around every brain.
parts.breaks: An emergency path that misses a need leaves agents frozen at the edge of a failure state with no audit trail — RECOVERY_TARGET/MEAL_ENERGY/EXHAUSTION constants are the tuning surface.
parts.whyScore: Focused 317-line module, zero panics in impl, tests cover energy emergencies and family precedence.

parts.label: outcome-memory modules (food/work/commitment)
parts.what: Four #[serde(skip)]-as-tail outcome memories: food_memory, forage_memory, work_memory, commitments — learn from resolved decisions, forgotten on death, serialized as checkpoint tails.
parts.why: The 'learning' half of NEAT+memory: brains see memory inputs fed by these stores.
parts.breaks: forget(i) must run on every death path — step() does it (lib.rs:2083-2089) but a death inside a domain module that skips the sweep leaks stale memory of a dead person.
parts.whyScore: Small focused modules (75–190 lines each), tail-serialized consistently, death-forget is centralized in the step sweep.

boundary.label: BOUNDARY
boundary.blurb: the crossings: XNS1/XNC1 wire encode, map_layers rasters, XXSAVE save codec + 31-version load ladder, legacy readers, Action enum

parts.label: viewer_snapshot — XNS1 bit-packed frames
parts.what: Builds one frame: XNS1 header (magic, version=2, paused flag, tick, counts) + JSON metadata + 16-byte person records + 16-byte animal records; coprime-stride sampling caps at 20k.
parts.why: Half of the wire contract — bit layout must agree with field.gd decode and the prose contract.
parts.breaks: Byte 12 packs action(low6)|rested(bit6)|grouped(bit7): a new Action ≥64 that misses the remap table silently corrupts the rested/grouped flags — the ceiling is a comment convention, not a check; `home as u8` is safe only because validate() caps markets ≤64.
parts.whyScore: Parity with the GDScript decoder verified end-to-end (connection_check + check_protocol header assertions); but the 6-bit action ceiling is enforced only by a comment + the remap match — mechanically unchecked (audit verified all 5 IDs >63 ARE remapped today).

parts.label: map_layers terrain/explored rasters
parts.what: On-request base64 raster packet: terrain classes/elevation/qi/regions + river polylines + region labels + fog-of-war chunk mask.
parts.why: Heavy static terrain travels once, not per-frame — the deliberate split out of the snapshot path.
parts.breaks: Class byte order must match Terrain enum declaration (Water0..River6) — mirrored by terrain_layer.gd TERRAIN_COLORS[7]; check_protocol asserts max(classes) ≤ 6 and exact raster sizes.
parts.whyScore: Verified by check_protocol.py:66-75 (768×480×4.0 raster, base64 lengths, class bound, explored chunk mask size); terrain only refreshes on request.

parts.label: checkpoint_payload + save — tuple tails
parts.what: postcard-serializes (World, memories, map, (explored, carcasses, spawns, spears, bows, hunting_stats, meat_trade, market_information, demand), (governance, rumours, water, traffic)) → zstd → XXSAVE34+len envelope → atomic tmp+rename write.
parts.why: Write-side of the save contract; the nested tuple ORDER is the schema — load's tail chain must walk it in exactly this order.
parts.breaks: Insert a field mid-tuple and every older-version tail read lands on the wrong type — loud for old headers (they branch before the tail) but the nesting order is the contract, mirrored nowhere outside this call and the load chain.
parts.whyScore: Round-trip + replay equality tested (checkpoint_replays_exactly, checkpoint_load_preserves_world_state_exactly); atomic write prevents torn checkpoints; tail order mirrors the load chain which the v12 fixture + synthetic header tests exercise.

parts.label: World::load — 31-version dispatch ladder
parts.what: ~540 lines dispatching on the 8-byte header: two format families (dev 20-29+34 read tuple+tails; release 19,30-33 read older tuple then remap Action variants 39-41; legacy 04-18 route to frozen readers), then ~10 per-version fixup gates (init_wildlife, upgrade_landscape, relocate_fertile_land, spawn init, governance_step…).
parts.why: The only path by which 31 save versions become one live World — the most failure-dense code in the repo.
parts.breaks: Every fixup gate is a hand-maintained header list — the SAME list recurs ~8 times in non-sequential order (19,30,31,20,21…34). Adding v35 means editing every list; forgetting one silently re-runs an init pass on a fresh save (animals respawn, forests move) — the test at lib.rs:4018 exists because this exact failure happened.
parts.whyScore: Silent-corruption surface: a missed header in a fixup gate doesn't error, it mutates valid state on load. Eight+ hand-repeated, non-sequential magic-byte lists, two Action-index families, and tail-parsing that must mirror checkpoint_payload's tuple order — with real-bytes coverage for exactly ONE of 31 versions.

parts.label: legacy_v4..v13 frozen readers
parts.what: Ten modules of frozen schema structs + From conversions for saves 04-13. v12/v13 froze Agents+Market (the types named in the architecture review); ~18 other nested types (Patch, Road, Person, Council, Graveyard, Farm, Tavern, Wildlife, Education, Urban, Banking, Genome, Innovations…) remain live imports.
parts.why: The migration half of the save ladder — each module pins a past World layout so current types can evolve.
parts.breaks: Any change to a still-live embedded type silently reinterprets old bytes or fails deserialize — only the v12 byte fixture stands between a Person/Urban/Wildlife field edit and real old saves; legacy_v4 and v5 have zero test lines.
parts.whyScore: Freeze job is half-done: Agents/Market got Legacy twins (review finding partially closed) but ~18 nested types are still shared; unit tests synthesize old bytes FROM current types, so they can't catch real-format drift. Coverage on real bytes exists only for v12.

parts.label: migrate_brain_schemas + neat-core input migration
parts.what: On load: detects 42/48-input genomes, shifts node IDs up to 52, migrates the three Innovation registries (world/council/wildlife), reconnects need/food-readiness inputs, then recompiles every brain.
parts.why: The schema bridge between old brains and the 52-sensor present — memory node IDs are pinned at u32::MAX-3.. so the shift can't collide.
parts.breaks: The registry and genome must migrate in the same pass (migrate_inputs + migrate_node_ids); doing one without the other desyncs innovation numbering — documented in code, done correctly, but order-sensitive.
parts.whyScore: Correct three-registry handling with a documented pairing requirement (neat-core lib.rs:553-555); needs_input_migration detection is by input count so already-migrated genomes don't double-shift; memory_and_species.rs + genome compile checks cover it.

transport.label: TRANSPORT
transport.blurb: the concurrency layer: TCP framing, client send/receive, readiness handshake, viewer reassembly

parts.label: messages/Client — frame reassembly + budgets
parts.what: 4-byte LE length-prefixed frames; 1MB command cap, 2MB input budget, 32-message batch cap, 8-deep reply queue, nonblocking read/write with partial-write offset tracking.
parts.why: The wire's moving floor — every command and snapshot rides this; it's also the only concurrency boundary in the server (single-threaded loop + Rayon inside step).
parts.breaks: Reply queue depth 8 with pop_front: a command flood drops the OLDEST replies — the client sees acks for later commands only; bounded by design but an aggressive script could lose its own ack.
parts.whyScore: Budgeted at every seam (frame 1MB, input 2MB, batch 32, queue 8) and unit-tested for partial-frame reassembly + oversize rejection (main.rs:735-752).

parts.label: XIANXIA_READY_FILE atomic readiness
parts.what: Backend binds port 0, writes {pid, port} to <path>.tmp then renames to the ready file; dev.py polls for the file and verifies the recorded pid equals the child's.
parts.why: Port-zero assignment + atomic discovery is what lets concurrent backends/tests coexist without port races — the isolation mechanism every test relies on.
parts.breaks: If the tmp+rename order flipped, launchers could read a half-written port; if the pid check were skipped, a stale ready file could bind a viewer to a dead port — both are correct today.
parts.whyScore: Atomic write-then-rename (main.rs:525-531) + pid verification in dev.py:80-88 + isolation test proves two backends get distinct ports and one dying leaves the other's save intact.

parts.label: main.gd TCP client — newest-frame-wins
parts.what: Polls socket, reassembles 4-byte-prefixed frames, buffers XNS1 frames and decodes only the NEWEST (drops stale snapshots), JSON-decodes XNC1 replies, reconnects every 2s.
parts.why: The client half of the conduit — drop-stale keeps an overloaded viewer from falling ever further behind.
parts.breaks: Frame length guard `4 <= len <= 4_194_304` mirrors no server constant — the server has NO snapshot size cap; a world whose metadata+records exceed 4MB triggers a reconnect loop the player sees as a hang; also on reconnect the viewer re-selects agent 0 silently.
parts.whyScore: Solid reassembly + stale-drop policy (main.gd:806-822) and it asserts full size agreement with the encoder (836-844); the 4MB bound is a viewer-side guess, not a shared constant — low-probability hang class, flagged not asserted.

parts.label: field.gd receive() — record decode
parts.what: Unpacks each 16-byte person record: id, xy, action&63 | rested&64 | grouped&128, kind&15 | carried&32 | hidden&64 | sleeping&128, health&127 | child&128, home byte; rebuilds spatial hash for picking.
parts.why: The decode half of the wire contract — the mirror that must match the Rust encoder bit-for-bit.
parts.breaks: Any encoder flag move silently misrenders (e.g. a shifted bit reads as 'rested' for everyone); no shared schema — parity rests on the protocol+connection tests and careful review.
parts.whyScore: Bit positions match the encoder exactly (verified in audit: byte12 action/64/128, byte13 kind/32/64/128, byte14 health/128, byte15 home); exercised live by connection_check — still a hand-mirrored decode across languages with no generated schema.

def connection_check(run):
    with server(backend(), run / "connected-viewer") as port:
        result = subprocess.run([godot(), "--headless", "--path", ROOT / "viewer", "--log-file",
                                 run / "connected-godot.log", "--script", "res://bench/connection_check.gd"],
                                env={**os.environ, "XIANXIA_PORT": str(port)}, capture_output=True,
                                text=True, errors="replace", timeout=35)
        output = result.stdout + result.stderr
        (run / "connected-viewer.txt").write_text(output, encoding="utf-8")
        if result.returncode or "SCRIPT ERROR" in output or "Verified connected Godot viewer" not in output:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Live viewer smoke check failed. See {run / 'connected-viewer.txt'}")

parts.label: birth/death → genome pool feedback
parts.what: The evolutionary loop: deaths free agent slots + memories; births run Genome::crossover(father, mother) + mutate_weights(0.15) + add_node(0.6) + compile → new brain; three independent Innovation registries keep node/gene numbering consistent per pool.
parts.why: The reason the conduit never stops: population turnover rewrites the very brains that generate candidate scores.
parts.breaks: Inheritance uses father-as-fitter unconditionally — fitness is genealogy, not measured success; neat_core::species() exists but is never called in production, so 'NEAT' here is crossover+mutation without speciation pressure.
parts.whyScore: The loop is real and replay-verified, but call it what it is: parent→child crossover+mutation, not full NEAT speciation — species() is dead production code (only tests reference it).

parts.label: neat-core — genome/compiled brain engine
parts.what: Independent crate: Genome/Innovations (historical edge/split tracking), feed-forward compile() with cycle/duplicate/budget checks, allocation-free evaluate(), crossover/mutate/input-schema migration, Rng (splitmix64).
parts.why: The brain substrate — three consumers (people, councils, wildlife) trust its invariants; 52-sensor schema with pinned memory node IDs at u32::MAX-3..
parts.breaks: compile() is the safety net: it rejects cycles, dup IDs, non-finite weights, input-count mismatch — a genome that compiles is safe to evaluate; anything the compile check misses lands in every tick's decision loop.
parts.whyScore: Clean separation, real validation at compile (lib.rs:333-411), MAX_NODES budget, memory IDs pinned outside the shiftable range (line 10-19), 131 test lines + dedicated tests crate.

parts.label: memory_pilot — experiment fused into hot path
parts.what: An A/B trial harness (Trial::adjust scores candidates from outcome memory) that lives inside World.watch and is consulted in request()'s scoring loop and execute_with_memory_pilot — an alternate execution path inside step().
parts.why: A research pilot riding production rails: when enabled it MUTATES candidate scores and swaps the executor — genuine dual-identity code sharing the production state type.
parts.breaks: With the trial active, decisions are scored by an experiment — the saved world remembers nothing about pilot state (watch is #[serde(skip)]), so a save/load boundary silently drops the trial while genomes may have been shaped by it; gated by Option but invisible in checkpoints.
parts.whyScore: Dual-identity fusion: an experimental scorer and an alternate executor share the production World and hot loops (request() at lib.rs:1804-1815, step at 2199-2203); bounded by an Option gate, but the pilot's influence on evolved genomes survives unsaved.

parts.label: tools/dev.py — verification harness
parts.what: Single local entry: doctor/test(sim,viewer,connection,protocol,replay,isolation,labs,world,all)/bench/soak/play/preview/package/queue + background isolation via source snapshots + per-run evidence dirs.
parts.why: The outer loop's conductor — every claim in the README maps to a suite here; CI runs `test all`.
parts.breaks: Server teardown is terminate→kill with a 10s window; a wedged backend gets SIGKILL — acceptable for tests but a hung step looks like a pass-fail coin flip rather than a watchdog report.
parts.whyScore: Real end-to-end coverage: replay SHA-256 equality, two-backend isolation with deliberate kill, bank+relationship protocol runs on the real fixture, headless Godot + live connection check — this is the loop that keeps the audit's greens honest.

parts.label: check_protocol.py — wire end-to-end
parts.what: Python client of the real TCP API: asserts frame/header layout, record counts, conservation accounts, map_layers raster sizes, sensor names/count, command semantics, save→step→load→step metadata equality, advance_days rollover.
parts.why: The independent consumer of the wire contract — it can't see Rust internals, so it only passes if the boundary is honest.
parts.breaks: 30-frame wait loops assume replies arrive in order; a dropped reply (8-deep queue overflow) reads as a test failure not a protocol error — fine for CI, ambiguous for diagnosis.
parts.whyScore: The deepest single check: header version + exact size equation (line 41), all-conservation invariants (50-53), map_layers dims + class bound + fog mask (66-75), 52 sensors with named tail (77-81), save/load metadata equality across ~16 collections (115-130).
